title: Conservation of Energy
seo_title: Conservation of Energy Worksheets: Roller Coasters, Falling Objects and Energy Tables (Physics)
standard_text: Create a computational model to calculate the change in the energy of one component in a system when the change in energy of the other component(s) and energy flows in and out of the system are known.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on conservation of energy (NGSS HS-PS3-1): energy tables, falling objects, roller coasters, pendulums and energy lost to friction. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy is never created or destroyed.
key_sub: PE + KE + thermal energy stays the same in a closed system.
body_html:
How to think about it

Total energy stays the same; it only changes form or moves.

  • No friction: PEtop + KEtop = PEbottom + KEbottom. Falling from rest: v = √(2gh).
  • With friction: some energy becomes thermal energy, but the total is still the same.
  • Energy table: PE + KE + thermal = total at every point.
Example

Dropped from 20 m. Speed at the bottom?

√(2 × 9.8 × 20)

Answer: 19.8 m/s

Example

PE 1,000 J at top, KE 850 J at bottom. Thermal?

1,000 − 850

Answer: 150 J

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy gets used up.
  • Thinking friction destroys energy.
  • Thinking heavier objects land faster (no air resistance).

faq.a: In a closed system, the total energy stays the same. It can change from one form to another, such as potential to kinetic.

faq.q: How fast does a dropped object land?
faq.a: Without air resistance, v = √(2gh). The mass does not matter.

faq.q: What happens to energy lost to friction?
faq.a: It is not destroyed. It becomes thermal energy (and a little sound) in the surfaces and the air.

items.q: Do a heavy ball and a light ball dropped from the same height land at the same speed (no air resistance)?
c: No, the heavy one is faster.
Yes, because mass cancels in mgh = ½mv².

items.e: All the PE (mgh = 245 J) becomes KE.

c: the sum of kinetic and potential energy

items.q: What does the law of conservation of energy say?
c: Energy is used up over time.
Energy can be created by machines.
